title: Antihypertensive effect of ragaglitazar: a novel PPARalpha and gamma dual activator.
text_summary: 本文发表于Pharmacological Research，评价PPARα/γ双重激动剂ragaglitazar在胰岛素抵抗和非胰岛素抵抗高血压动物模型中的降压及内皮保护作用。研究在Zucker fa/fa大鼠、自发性高血压大鼠、双肾一夹型高血压大鼠和正常血压WKY大鼠中比较ragaglitazar与吡格列酮。ragaglitazar降低多种高血压模型的收缩压，同时改善甘油三酯、胰岛素水平及乙酰胆碱诱导的主动脉舒张，但不降低正常大鼠血压。作者认为其降压作用可能同时涉及胰岛素敏感性改善、脂质调节和内皮功能恢复。

Pharmacological Research 54 (2006) 129–135
Antihypertensive effect of ragaglitazar:
An o v e lP P A R/H9251and /H9253dual activator
Prem K. Mamnoor, Pragathi Hegde, Srinivas R. Datla, Ravi K.B. Damarla,
Ramanujam Rajagopalan, Ranjan Chakrabarti∗
Discovery Biology, Dr . Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd.-Discovery Research, 7-1-27 Ameerpet, Hyderabad 500016, India
Accepted 23 March 2006
Abstract
Ragaglitazar is a novel and potent dual peroxisome proliferators activated receptor (PPAR)/H9251and /H9253activator. The aim of this study is to investigate
the effect of ragaglitazar on blood pressure and endothelial function in insulin resistant animal model and non-insulin resistant hypertensive models.
The effects ragaglitazar were tested in Zucker fa/fa, spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR), 2 kidney 1clip rat (2K1C) and Wistar Kyoto rats (WKY).
Pioglitazone was taken as a comparative standard. Ragaglitazar showed signiﬁcant reduction (P < 0.001) of systolic blood pressure (SBP) in insulin
resistant fa/fa rats, with concomitant reduction in plasma triglycerides (TG) and insulin levels while pioglitazone (10 mg kg
−1) showed signiﬁcant
(P < 0.05) but comparatively less reduction. Ragaglitazar in contrast to pioglitazone showed signiﬁcant reduction (P < 0.05) of SBP in SHR, 2K1C
while the same dose did not have any effect on normotensive WKY . Ragaglitazar also showed signiﬁcant improvement in acetylcholine-induced
relaxation in isolated aorta of Zucker fa/fa, SHR, 2K1C and also potentiated the insulin-induced vasorelaxation in Zucker fa/fa rats. These ﬁndings
summarize that ragaglitazar shows signiﬁcant reduction of BP and improvement in endothelial function not only in insulin resistant but also in
non-insulin resistant hypertensive models where standard thiazolidinediones are ineffective. These data indicates that dual PPAR/H9251and /H9253activator
ragaglitazar can be beneﬁcial for the treatment of hypertension and vascular disease commonly associated with type 2 diabetes.

Keywords: Ragaglitazar; Peroxisome proliferators activated receptor (PPAR); Hypertension
1. Introduction
Peroxisome proliferator activated receptors (PPARs) are lig-
and activated transcription factors expressed in three isoforms
PPAR/H9251,P P A R/H9253, and PPAR /H9254, encoded by separate genes [1].
Blood glucose levels and insulin sensitivity can be improved
by treatment with PPAR /H9253ligand thiazolidinediones. On the
other hand, increased triglycerides and decreased high-density
lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, which is the most common lipid
abnormalities in patients with type 2 diabetes, can be effectively
altered by treatment with PPAR /H9251ligands [2]. Ragaglitazar an
alkoxy propionic acid derivative is a novel peroxisome prolifer-
ator activated receptor (PPAR)/H9251and /H9253agonist with potent lipid
lowering and insulin sensitizing activity in animal models and
type 2 diabetes patients [3–5].

Clinically available PPAR/H9253agonists like rosiglitazone and
pioglitazone are insulin sensitizing antidiabetic drugs used as
mono therapy or in combination with other antidiabetic drugs
[6]. Clinical and epidemiological studies have provided evidence
that a correlation exists between insulin resistance and essential
hypertension [7]. Endothelial dysfunction plays a key role in
pathogenesis of diabetic vascular disease. Impaired endothelial
function results from obesity associated with insulin resistance,
if untreated ultimately predispose the person to hypertension and
vascular disease [8]. Recent genetic analysis showed that two
dominant negative mutations in the ligand-binding domain of
PPAR/H9253were associated with severe insulin resistance and hyper-
tension in humans[9]. Consistent with this ﬁnding, PPAR/H9253ago-
nists showed blood pressure lowering effect in diabetic patients
[10].
Lipid lowering ﬁbrate classes of drugs are PPAR/H9251agonists,
known to show insulin sensitization, improvement in endothe-
lial function and reduction of blood pressure in humans[11–13].
It has been hypothesized that impaired endothelium-dependent
vasodilatation might be a consequence of hyperlipidemia and

thereby lipid lowering may provide an additional method of cor-
recting hypertension in high-risk patients [14]. Clinically used
PPAR ligands are reported to show efﬁcacy in various animal
models of hypertension [15–25].
There is an unmet medical need for the development of antidi-
abetic drugs that treat not only hyperglycemia but also other
components of metabolic syndrome, specially dyslipidemia and
hypertension. Thiazolidinediones like rosiglitazone and piogli-
tazone can markedly reduce insulin resistance but have modest
effects on plasma lipids in type 2 diabetic patients [26]. Taken
into consideration of probable beneﬁcial effect of dual PPAR
modulation on vascular system, we had initiated a study to
explore the antihypertensive property of ragaglitazar as com-
pared to pioglitazone and fenoﬁbrate in different animal models
of hypertension.
2. Materials and methods
2.1. Animals
Male Zucker fa/fa rats (15 weeks age), Zucker lean rats (15
weeks age), were obtained from Charles River, USA. Male
SHR (13 weeks age) and WKY (13 weeks age) were obtained
from Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories Ltd.-Discovery Research animal
facility. 2K1C Reno vascular hypertensive model was devel-
oped as described previously[27] and the animals were allowed
to recover for 15 days before starting the treatment. The ani-
mals were housed in standard laboratory conditions under a
controlled temperature (22 ± 1
◦C), humidity (60%), and 12 h
dark–light cycle. Drinking water and standard laboratory chow
(National Institution of Nutrition, Hyderabad, India) were sup-
plied ad lib through out the study period. The study design and
the experimental protocol were approved by the institutional
animal ethics committee (Discovery Research, Dr Reddy’s Lab-
oratories, Hyderabad) and as per the international rule.
2.2. Drugs and chemicals
Phenylephrine (Phe), acetylcholine (Ach), sodiumnitroprus-
side (SNP) was purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, USA).
Enalapril maleate was purchased from Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories
(Bulk Unit), India. All the compounds were dissolved in distilled
water and insulin (Sigma) was dissolved in 0.01 N HCL (ﬁnal
concentrations were adjusted to bath volume). Ragaglitazar and
pioglitazone were prepared by Discovery chemistry group at Dr.
Reddy’s Lab.-Discovery Research by published procedure and
were suspended in 0.25% (wt. vol
−1) carboxymethyl cellulose
and the dose volume was adjusted to 10 ml kg −1. Fenoﬁbrate
was obtained from Biocon (Bangalore, India). Other chemicals
were of analytical grade, obtained from Qualigens ﬁne chemi-
cals.
2.3. Experimental design/drug treatment
The animals were selected and randomized in-group of
ﬁve to six animals each. Zucker fa/fa rats were treated orally
with ragaglitazar and pioglitazone at 10 mg kg
−1 for 12 days.
SHR were treated with ragaglitazar, pioglitazone and enalapril
maleate (10 mg kg−1) and fenoﬁbrate (60 mg kg −1) orally for
21 days. Similarly 2K1C rats were treated with ragaglitazar,
pioglitazone and enalapril maleate, all at 10 mg kg
−1 orally for
21 days. Normotensive WKY were treated with ragaglitazar
(10 mg kg
−1) orally for 21 days. BP of untreated Zucker lean
rats was also monitored.
2.4. Blood pressure measurement
The rats were initially trained to the non-invasive blood pres-
sure system for BP measurements three times on alternate days
for 1 week, before base line BP were measured. The experimen-
tal rats were randomized based on SBP. BP was measured in a
conscious state by tail cuff method (IITC model 31 computerized
blood pressure analyzer; IITC Life Science instruments, Wood-
land Hills, CA, USA) after stabilizing the animals in restrainers
for 25 min at 34
◦C. The BP was measured 1 h after the drug
administration. BP was monitored weekly twice in all the groups
2.5. Blood sampling and analytical methods
Blood samples were collected from retro orbital plexus of
anesthetized rats on ﬁnal day. The plasma insulin was measured
using rat radioimmunoassay kit (Linco Research Lab, USA).
Plasma TG was measured using an auto analyzer (Vita lab, Selec-
tra).
2.6. V ascular reactivity studies
Thoracic aorta from treated animals and control was excised
and dissected free of connective tissue and placed in krebs-
Hensleit solution as described by us previously [28]. Endothe-
lium dependent relaxation was assessed with cumulative
doses of Ach (10
−9–10−5 mol L−1) after pre-contraction with
10−6 mol L−1 Phe. Endothelium independent relaxation was
assessed with cumulative doses of SNP (10−9–10−5 mol L−1).
The insulin sensitization effect, represented by attenuation
of agonist induced contraction [29,30], was measured in the
isolated aorta from treated Zucker fa/fa. After assessing the
endothelial integrity, the aortic rings were pre-incubated with
insulin at a concentration of 50 mU L
−1 for 10 min. Phe dose
response curve (10−9–10−5 mol L−1) was established.
2.7. Calculations and statistical analysis
The contractions were recorded as mg tension generated
at each dose. Relaxation to agonists in isolated vessels was
given as percent relaxation in rings pre-contracted with Phe.
Results are expressed as mean ± S.E. Maximal relaxation
or contraction ( E
max) was determined for each individual
concentration–response curve by non-linear regression analy-
sis with the use of sigma plot software. Percent reduction was
calculated using the following formulae:
Percent reduction (%)
= [1 − (ﬁnal day treated mean)/ﬁnal day control mean]×100

3. Results
3.1. Effect of ragaglitazar on blood pressure and plasma
parameters
Zucker fa/fa showed signiﬁcant increase (P < 0.001) in SBP,
plasma TG and plasma insulin levels compared to the lean
Zucker rats ( Table 1). Ragaglitazar treatment in Zucker fa/fa
showed a signiﬁcant decrease (P < 0.001) in SBP (21%), plasma
TG (77%) and plasma insulin (93%). Pioglitazone when tested
at similar dose for comparison, showed relatively less effect
on SBP (10%), but signiﬁcant effect ( P < 0.05) on plasma TG
(49%) and plasma insulin (66%) ( Table 1). Ragaglitazar treat-
ment in SHR, 2K1C rats showed signiﬁcant reduction (P < 0.05)
in SBP (13% and 27% respectively) compared to untreated rats.
Pioglitazone treatment failed to show signiﬁcant reduction in
both the models. Enalapril maleate showed signiﬁcant reduction
(P < 0.001) of SBP (20%) in SHR and (37%) in 2K1C respec-
tively (Table 2). In SHR, fenoﬁbrate did not show any effect on
BP so vascular studies were not performed. Ragaglitazar did not
show any modulation of SBP in WKY (Table 2).
3.2. Effect of ragaglitazar on Ach and SNP induced
relaxation in aortic rings
Insulin resistant Zucker fa/fa in conjunction with hyperten-
sion, exhibited impaired Ach induced relaxation (E
max 31 ± 3%,
P < 0.0001) compared to normotensive Zucker lean aortic prepa-
ration ( Emax 69 ± 2%). Ragaglitazar treatment signiﬁcantly
improved Ach induced relaxation in fa/fa rats ( Emax 58 ± 2%,
P < 0.001) (Fig. 1). Pioglitazone treatment also resulted in sim-
ilar but signiﬁcantly less improvement of endothelial relaxation
(E
max 42 ± 3%, P < 0.05). Similarly non-insulin resistant hyper-

4. Discussion
Diabetes is a multi pathophysiological disease, which man-
ifests in the form of not only hyperglycemia, but with other
complications. Insulin resistance is considered as the underly-
ing cause of type 2 diabetes. Insulin is being a major regulatory
hormone in a variety of metabolic and cell signaling process,
and its resistance in different target organs led to several dis-
ease conditions. Dyslipidemia and hypertension are two major
abnormalities, which are found to be associated with a majority
of type 2 diabetic patients [31].
Hypertension in diabetes is associated with impaired
endothelium dependent vascular relaxation to insulin [32].
Upon binding to the endothelial insulin receptor, insulin acti-
vates endothelial NO system (eNOS), stimulating release of
endothelium-derived nitric oxide (NO) resulting in vasodilata-
tion, which would tend to control blood pressure [33]. Vasodi-
latation is impaired in insulin resistance state leading to hyper-
tension. Diabetic patients are at high risk for atherosclerosis and
myocardial infarction and some of this risk can be attributed to
diabetic dyslipidemia, which is characterized by high triglyc-
eride, low HDL and increased small dense LDL-cholesterol
which in turn leads to the deposition of cholesterol in artery
thereby impairing its normal function [34].
PPAR/H9253ligands rosiglitazone and pioglitazone have being
introduced in the market as insulin sensitizers for the treatment
of type 2 diabetes, but their effect on dyslipidemia is not up to the
expectation. Rosiglitazone does not signiﬁcantly improve lipid
levels [31], whereas pioglitazone has been reported to have very
moderate effect [35].
PPAR/H9251is considered to be mainly involved in the metabolism
of lipid and thereby its modulation will lead to better reduction
of lipid proﬁle [36]. Recent reports have also indicated the ben-
eﬁcial effect of PPAR/H9251modulation on insulin resistance [37].
We have reported previously that ragaglitazar, a dual agonist of
PPAR/H9251and /H9253shows signiﬁcantly better effect to hyperglycemia,
insulin resistance and dyslipidemia including HDL-cholesterol
elevation than any marketed PPAR ligands. It was shown that
ragaglitazar induce downstream genes of both PPAR /H9251(ACO
mRNA) and PPAR /H9253(aP2 mRNA) at efﬁcacy dose in animal
models [3,4]. We have extended our study with this compound
to explore its effect on hypertension and vascular reactivity, an
integral dysfunction of metabolic syndrome.
Zucker fa/fa rats are obese, insulin resistant, dyslipidemic
and hypertensive thereby ideal model for metabolic syndrome.
In preliminary studies carried out with different doses of
ragaglitazar in Zucker fa/fa, BP reduction was observed at
3m gk g
−1 itself (138 mmHg), but optimum BP lowering effect
was observed at 10 mg kg−1. Accordingly in all studies reported
here, ragaglitazar was used at 10 mg kg −1 doses. In fa/fa rats,
ragaglitazar showed better insulin sensitizing, lipid lowering and
antihypertensive effect than pioglitazone. Our data in Zucker
fa/fa rats differs from a recent report in ZDF rats, where ragagli-
tazar and pioglitazone showed similar insulin sensitivity and
lipid lowering effect [38]. This discrepancy may be due to dif-
ferent models and especially in ZDF rats hyperglycemia adds
to the complexity of overall metabolic abnormalities. To under-
stand the antihypertensive action of ragaglitazar, we studied its
action on vascular reactivity. Zucker fa/fa rats demonstrated vas-
cular dysfunction, like decreased acetylcholine-induced relax-
ation and reduced ability of insulin to attenuate phenylephrine-
induced vasoconstriction in contrast to lean Zucker rats. The
antihypertensive activity of ragaglitazar is well correlated with
the signiﬁcant improvement in vascular function by correcting
the Ach induced endothelium dependent vasorelaxation as well
as insulin induced vasorelaxation. Pioglitazone showed less but
signiﬁcant improvement in Ach induced relaxation in these rats.
Blood pressure lowering was observed after 7 days of treatment
with ragaglitazar in this model, so the studies were performed
for 12 days to have the plateau effect.
After observing the antihypertensive effect of ragaglitazar
in insulin resistant animal models, we extended our study to
non-insulin resistant models of hypertension. SHR are well-
established genetic model of hypertension. Although some of
the investigators have reported presence of insulin resistance in
SH rats, we did not observe any signiﬁcant insulin resistance
in SH rats from our colony, both by plasma insulin levels and
also by euglycemic clamp studies (data not shown). Ragaglitazar
showed signiﬁcant reduction in SBP and also improved endothe-
lial dysfunction in these rats. Pioglitazone and ﬁbrates on the
other hand failed to show any effect. Pioglitazone and fenoﬁbrate
are reported to show efﬁcacy in animal models of hypertension
at higher dose or with prolonged treatment [21–23]. It might be
possible that dual activation of PPAR /H9251and /H9253by ragaglitazar
leads to better efﬁcacy in this model in short duration treat-
ment compared to fenoﬁbrate (PPAR /H9251ligand) or pioglitazone
(PPAR/H9253ligand). We observed signiﬁcant blood pressure reduc-
tion in SHR only at the end of 14 days of treatment, so the study
was extended till 21 days to conﬁrm the plateauing of the effect.
Normotensive WKY or SD rats did not show any change in
blood pressure after ragaglitazar treatment. It has been reported
that blood vessel of SHR expresses higher levels of PPAR/H9251and
PPAR/H9253than WKY which plays an important role in vascular
changes during development of hypertension [39]. The blood
pressure lowering potential of ragaglitazar in fa/fa rats were
more prominent than in SHR. Insulin resistance and dyslipi-
demia play major role in vascular dysfunction in fa/fa rats, but
may not be in SHR. Ragaglitazar, has shown improvement in
both of these parameters, which may explain its pronounced
improvement of vascular function in fa/fa rats. Results from
SHR indicate that ragaglitazar has some unique effect on vas-
cular function, which is independent of its insulin sensitizing
and lipid lowering action. To reconﬁrm antihypertensive activ-
ity of ragaglitazar, we decided to study its action in a totally
different kind of hypertensive model-renovascular hypertensive
(2K1C) rats. Even in this model, ragaglitazar showed signiﬁcant
reduction in SBP. As expected pioglitazone failed to show any
effect.
Although it is not clear how ragaglitazar is showing its effect,
we believe several factors arising from the dual PPAR /H9251and /H9253
activation can be responsible for it. We have shown that dual

134 P .K. Mamnoor et al. / Pharmacological Research 54 (2006) 129–135
activation of /H9251and /H9253have lead to better insulin sensitizing
activity of ragaglitazar, which might in turn help its antihy-
pertensive action. It is also known that PPAR /H9251is involved in
mitochondrial fatty acid /H9252-oxidation, a critical fuel generating
mechanism in the heart [40]. Generation of reactive oxygen
species (ROS) is considered as a major force for several vascular
dysfunctions in diabetes patients [41] and it has been reported
that PPAR agonists play an important role in improving this sit-
uation. Various lipoproteins (LDL, HDL) and apolipoproteins
(ApoA1, ApoE) have been reported to affect vascular endothe-
lium function either through eNOS or other signaling pathway
[42]. This in turn affects vascular contraction and relaxation
ability. PPAR/H9251ligands are reported to improve the lipid pro-
ﬁle and endothelial dysfunction in metabolic syndrome patients
[43]. Ragaglitazar due to its dual PPAR activation shows sig-
niﬁcant improvement in plasma lipid proﬁle that may lead to
beneﬁcial effect on vascular function. Angiotensin II can cause
insulin resistance and there is some evidence for increased renin
angiotensin system (RAS) components in the models tested in
our study [44,45]. There are several reports of PPAR activa-
tion modulating angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression and
repressing signal transduction through this receptor to suppress
vascular remodeling, lesion formation, and oxidative stress[46].
It is possible that a part of ragaglitazar effect is mediated by the
modulation of renin angiotensin system in these models. Fur-
ther studies are needed to understand the exact mechanism of
ragaglitazar action.
Studies with PPAR ligands have shown that both PPAR /H9251
and /H9253can have beneﬁcial effects on oxidative stress in the vas-
cular wall and also prevent the vascular increase of superoxide
anion production[47]. There is a possibility that in these models,
dual PPAR action of ragaglitazar is responsible for its bene-
ﬁcial effect. Although enalapril maleate works through ACE
inhibition, we used it as a reference standard to ensure the
proper functioning of experimental setup. Ragaglitazar appears
to improve fatty liver in fat fed rats without producing the hep-
atomegaly and also the antihypertensive effects of ragaglitazar
may not be related to the side effects reported in animals[48–50].
In summary, our studies in three different type of hyper-
tensive models clearly indicate that the antihypertensive action
and improvement of vascular function by ragaglitazar cannot
be explained just by its insulin sensitizing activity as might be
with pioglitazone. At this juncture, we are not clear about the
mechanism of such unique antihypertensive property of ragagli-
tazar. As described earlier PPAR /H9251and PPAR/H9253agonists have
been shown to produce variety of effects such as antiprolif-
erative action, protection from oxidative damage and action
on various inﬂammatory modulators in cardiac tissues [51].I t
is exciting to speculate that dual activation of PPAR /H9251and /H9253
might produce some direct beneﬁcial effects on vascular sys-
tem, which might give added advantage to the patients with
metabolic syndrome. There is also a possibility that ragagli-
tazar might have some direct effect on classical pathways like
Ca
2+ efﬂux or stimulation of NO production by endothelium
and thereby exert its vasorelaxant property. Further studies are
in progress to establish the mechanism of the antihypertensive
action of ragaglitazar.

image_summary: 第1页：论文首页，含题名、作者和摘要，概述ragaglitazar在多种大鼠模型中的降压与内皮效应。
第2页：引言与方法，介绍PPAR双重激动机制、动物模型、给药设计、血压测量和离体血管实验。
第3页：结果表格与曲线页，列出收缩压及代谢参数，并展示不同模型的剂量反应和血压变化。
第4页：结果曲线页，比较ragaglitazar和吡格列酮对不同高血压模型主动脉乙酰胆碱舒张反应的影响。
第5页：结果续页与讨论起始，描述内皮依赖性舒张改善并讨论胰岛素抵抗、脂质和血压的联系。
第6页：讨论续页，分析PPARα/γ共同激活、内皮功能恢复及不同模型中降压效应的可能机制。
第7页：讨论结尾与参考文献，概括ragaglitazar的实验性降压作用及相关PPAR研究。
